## 4. Architektur (Kurzfassung — Details `docs/02-architecture.md`, Ist-Stand `docs/11-mvp-status.md`)

```
Brief ──► LLM-Extraktion (Referenz, Stichtag, Firma, USt-Id, Site-Rollen, autorisierte Absender je Thema)
   │
   ▼
Orchestrator (asyncio, Blackboard = append-only Extraktionen mit URL)
  ├─ Mission tender         (Browser 1)  → positions, clarifications
  ├─ Mission specification  (Browser 2)  → spec_revisions, requirements     ──┐
  ├─ Mission mail           (Browser 4)  → mail_list, mail_message           │
  └─ Missionen erp:<Gruppe> (Browser 3, je Kataloggruppe ein Tab) ◄─────────┘ (starten, sobald Spezifikation fertig)
       Explorer-Tools: click · type · select(+then_click) · fill_fields · check · set_slider · open_url · back
                       · read_all_pages(next_ref) · extract(kind) · extract_urls(urls, kind) · finish
       Fortschritts-Checkliste je Mission (vom Code aus dem Blackboard) → Auto-Finish, kein Wiederholen
   ▼
rules/resolve.py (deterministisch) → Answer + Trace → submit.py (Formular, TAN, confirm) 
```

Kernprinzipien:
- **LLM navigiert und interpretiert, Python rechnet.** Keine Arithmetik im LLM.
- **Observation = eigener DOM-Serializer** (a11y-basiert, alle Frames, Tooltips + geschlossene `<details>` sichtbar,
  `aria-hidden`/`display:none`-Köder raus, Canvas/`role=img` über `aria-label`, Zero-Width-Zeichen entfernt).
  Screenshots nur als Fallback für Vision (Qwen ist multimodal).
- **Jede Zahl hat Provenienz** (Quelle + Rohtext + Locale). Resolver wendet „neuester datierter Eintrag ≤ Stichtag,
  exakte Referenz, autorisierter Absender“ deterministisch an.
- **Immer eine Antwort abgeben.** Deadline-Wächter: spätestens bei `expires_at − 4 min` mit bestem Stand signieren.
  Leere Felder = 0 Punkte, falsche Felder = 0 Punkte → immer beste Schätzung eintragen, Positionen nie auslassen,
  außer sie lassen sich technisch nicht konfigurieren.

## 5. Workstreams & Branches (Details + Schnittstellen: `docs/07-workstreams.md`)

| Branch | Owner-Rolle | Liefert |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `feat/agent-orchestrator` | Orchestrierung & LLM | `contract.py`, `llm/`, `agents/orchestrator.py`, `explorer.py`, Deadline, Logging, Package-Layout `agent/` |
| `feat/browser-tools` | Browser-Robustheit | `browser/*` (Serializer, Actions, Guards, Documents), Fixture-Tests gegen `dev/fixtures` |
| `feat/tender-specification` | Vergabe + Spezifikation | Missionen + Fact-Schemas für Tender, LV, Bieterfragen, Spezifikation/Revisionen, Nachträge |
| `feat/erp-mail-evidence` | ERP + Mail | Missionen + Fact-Schemas für Material/Bestand/Konditionen, Mail-Freigaben, Keys |
| `feat/pricing-submission` | Rechnen + Abgabe | `rules/*` (Parser, Resolver, Pricing, Validate), `submit/*` (Konfigurator, TAN) |

Schnittstelle zwischen Explorern und Regeln sind die Extraktions-Schemata `KINDS` in `agent/rfq/agent/prompts.py`
(Owner: pricing-submission + orchestrator; Änderungen per PR). Alle Branches bitte auf `main` rebasen — das MVP liegt dort.

## 6. Arbeitsweise

- Python 3.12, `uv`, asyncio, Playwright (async), `openai` SDK (für Qwen, OpenAI-kompatibel). Keine pydantic-Abhängigkeit (noch nicht nötig).
  Keine weiteren schweren Abhängigkeiten ohne Absprache (Setup max. 5 min, Package ≤ 20 MB).
- Geld & Mengen: **`decimal.Decimal`**, niemals `float`. Rundung `ROUND_HALF_UP` exakt dort, wo die Regeln es sagen.
- Zahlen/Datum immer über `rules/parse.py` (Locale-Tags `(de-DE)`/`(en-US)`, `(TT/MM)`/`(MM/TT)`, Zeitzonen).
- Logging: jede LLM-Antwort, jede Aktion, jeder Fact als JSON-Zeile auf stdout (die Plattform zeigt stdout im Run-Log).
  Keine Secrets loggen. Format: `{"t":…,"agent":…,"event":…,…}`.
- Prompts liegen in `agent/rfq/agent/prompts.py`, sind **site-agnostisch** und enthalten nur Regeln,
  Glossar und Vorgehen — nie Public-Werte.
- Kleine PRs, je Branch eigener Bereich; `facts.py` und Prompts nur per Review ändern.
- Commits: aussagekräftig, Englisch, Imperativ.

## 7. Testen (Details: `docs/06-testing.md`)

1. `cd agent && uv run pytest -q` — Unit-Tests (Parser, Pricing, Resolver, Serializer) mit synthetischen Daten.
2. `uv run pytest dev/tests -q` — Fixture-Tests gegen gespeichertes Public-HTML (Fallen-Regression).
3. Lokal End-to-End: Terminal 1 `atira models proxy`; Terminal 2 `eval "$(atira scout --env)" && cd agent && uv run python main.py`
   (lokal wird nichts gewertet; Abgabe mit Scouting-Logins wird „acknowledged“, zählt nie).
4. `uv run python dev/eval/score.py <answer.json>` — Feldweise Bewertung gegen `dev/oracle` (Punkteschema der Challenge).
5. Sandbox: `atira test-run ./agent` → Punkte je Feld; Debug über `atira mcp` (`diagnose_run`, `run_logs`, `run_screenshot`).
6. Robustheit: Perturbations-Tests (umbenannte Labels, andere Reihenfolge, andere Locale) — Ziel privater Datensatz.

**Definition of Done** für jedes Feature: Unit-Test grün · keine Public-Werte in `agent/` (`dev/check_no_leaks.py`) ·
läuft lokal gegen Scouting-Sites · Logs nachvollziehbar.

# Team evals

An eval is your own world for the challenge: a web app with up to four sites, a task and its one correct answer. The
platform hosts it and runs agents on it, yours or, once you make it public, every team's, each on its own
leaderboard. Use it to test your agent on cases the public scenario doesn't have.

## Quickstart

```sh
atira eval init my-eval          # the starter kit: four sites, a bid configurator, BRIEF.md, expected.json
atira eval dev my-eval           # run it here; each answer is scored against expected.json and printed
```

- Keep `package-lock.json` in the folder: `npm ci` needs it.
- `next/font/google` works: a build reaches the package registries and Google Fonts, nothing else, and the running
  app reaches nothing.
- With its `node_modules`, a plain app is about 90 MB compressed (`.next/cache` is left out). The platform keeps a

starts and uses about 130 MB of a world's 2 GB.

Each version runs in **one permanent VM, its world**, from the moment its build is ready. Agents and you open its sites
directly on their public URLs; there is no gateway in front. Your app signs agents in and hands their answer in
itself, through two platform endpoints, the way the challenge's own sites do. The starter kit's `atira-kit.js` does
both: copy it into your app.

The app starts with, `<NAME>` being the site's name upper-cased with `_` for `-`:

| Variable | What |
| --- | --- |
| `PORT_<NAME>` | the port to listen on; use it rather than the manifest's |

- `POST $ATIRA_API_URL/v1/eval-worlds/verify` `{"site": "portal", "username": "u_…", "password": "…"}`: 200

  signed cookie and ask again at most every 10 s, so an ended run is signed out.
- `POST $ATIRA_API_URL/v1/eval-worlds/answer` `{"run_id": "run_…", "bid": {…}}` (or `preview_id`): for a run `202`
  and the run ends; for a preview `200` `{"accepted": true, "score": {"quality", "eligible", "breakdown"}}` and you can
  submit again; `400` `{"issues": [{"path", "message"}]}` for a bid that fails the answer schema, so the page can show
  them and the agent can try again; `409` once the run has its answer.

### Next.js

Copy `atira-kit.js` next to your app (it is plain Node, ESM), then a sign-in route, a guard and an answer route:

```ts
// app/login/route.ts: POST username, password (and returnTo) from your login page's form

export async function POST(request: Request) {
  const form = await request.formData()
  const signed = await signIn("web", String(form.get("username")), String(form.get("password")), true)
  if (!signed) return Response.redirect(new URL("/login?error=1", request.url), 303)
  return new Response(null, { status: 303, headers: { location: "/", "set-cookie": signed.cookie } })
}

// in a server component or route handler: the login, or off to /login
import { cookies } from "next/headers"
import { redirect } from "next/navigation"
import { currentLogin } from "@/atira-kit.js"
const login = await currentLogin((await cookies()).toString(), "web")

import { currentLogin, submitAnswer } from "@/atira-kit.js"
export async function POST(request: Request) {
  const login = await currentLogin(request.headers.get("cookie"), "web")
  if (!login) return Response.json({ error: "Bitte anmelden." }, { status: 401 })
```

answered), as the starter kit's `server.js` does.

## The answer

It is scored with the main challenge's scorer, against your `expected.json`: the decision must match; then the tender
reference 5 points, the discount 5, the net total 15 (it must also be the sum of the lines) and 75 for the positions,
shared equally, each split into material 35 %, quantity 20 %, unit price 30 % and lead time 15 %. A line for a
position your answer doesn't have costs one position's share. Breakdown fields such as `base_unit_price` are
accepted and not scored.

## Runs, previews and leaderboards

- `atira eval preview` gives you logins per site on the eval's one world for a few hours (`--hours`, 1–8), at once;
  nothing boots for it, and the world is never restarted on request. A bid you submit there is scored against
  `expected.json`.

  run's (`test`), any earlier submission's or run's of your team by its id (`--package sub_...` or `run_...`, scored or
  not, as long as its package is still stored), or a folder (`--package ./my-agent`), 1–3 times (`--repeats`). Name an
  entry with `--label`, or later with `atira run name <run> "name"` (only your team sees names). Each run is an ordinary run: its page,
  logs, screenshots and `diagnose_run` work as for test runs, with the scored run's 20-minute limit.

  team. Public ones: any team runs on them and reads their source, `expected.json`
  included. Each version has its own leaderboard (`atira eval board`): each team's best entry, by mean quality, then
  cost × time.

previews for up to 8 hours. Eval runs share your team's test-run limit: up to 12 test and eval
runs at a time and 12 waiting, together.

## Security

  the environment, never from the bundle.

- One world serves every run of the version: keep each run's state apart (by its run id).

accepted and not scored.

  the environment, never from the bundle.
- A private eval's sites get unguessable URLs; a public eval's are named after its slug.
- One world serves every run of the version: keep each run's state apart (by its run id).

position your answer doesn't have costs one position's share. Breakdown fields such as `base_unit_price` are
accepted and not scored.

## Runs, previews and leaderboards

- `atira eval preview` gives you logins per site on the eval's one world for a few hours (`--hours`, 1–8), at once;
  nothing boots for it, and the world is never restarted on request. A bid you submit there is scored against
  `expected.json`.
- `atira eval run` runs a package: your latest submission's (`--package submission`, the default), your latest test
  run's (`test`), any earlier submission's or run's of your team by its id (`--package sub_...` or `run_...`, scored or
  not, as long as its package is still stored), or a folder (`--package ./my-agent`), 1–3 times (`--repeats`). Name an
  entry with `--label`, or later with `atira run name <run> "name"` (only your team sees names). Each run is an ordinary run: its page,
  logs, screenshots and `diagnose_run` work as for test runs, with the scored run's 20-minute limit.
- Private evals (the default) are yours alone, their runs too: a run's page and logs answer 404 to anyone outside your
  team. Public ones: any team runs on them and reads their source, `expected.json`
  included. Each version has its own leaderboard (`atira eval board`): each team's best entry, by mean quality, then
  cost × time.

Limits, unless the organizers change them: 10 evals a team and 12 eval runs an hour (each repeat counts), and
previews for up to 8 hours. Eval runs share your team's test-run limit: up to 12 test and eval
runs at a time and 12 waiting, together.

## Security

- The world reaches only the platform's API (`ATIRA_API_URL`): everything else it needs is in the bundle or made by
  `build`.
- Every page should need a login: the sites are on public URLs. The starter kit's `atira-kit.js` does it, verifying
  each login with the platform.
- A public eval's source is public, `expected.json` included: never put a secret in it. `ATIRA_EVAL_TOKEN` comes from
  the environment, never from the bundle.
- A private eval's sites get unguessable URLs; a public eval's are named after its slug.
- One world serves every run of the version: keep each run's state apart (by its run id).
"}

docs/reference/atira-llms-full.txt:105:Your agent reads a public tender, finds the current specification, checks prices and stock in the ERP, looks up the approved discount in the sales inbox and submits one signed bid. Bring any frontier model, your own tools and prompts, up to four browsers in parallel; no human in the loop. Or use [ours](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/start#models): unlimited Qwen3.8-Flash-Next and Cloudflare Clef inference. Free for you. Each call still adds its simulated price to your run's cost, so the cost ranking stays fair. Every scored submission runs once on the public dataset. Eligible answers rank first, then higher quality, then lower cost × time. When the hackathon ends, every team's latest submission that passed review runs once by default, or best of three if the team opts in before the final run starts, on a private dataset. We pick the winners on three things, roughly in this order: performance on the private dataset, performance on the public dataset, and the elegance of the system.
docs/reference/atira-llms-full.txt:113:[Sign in with GitHub](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/login?next=/team) and create a team of up to 5. Invite teammates by their GitHub username on [your team page](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/team); each invite works only for that account.
docs/reference/atira-llms-full.txt:117:The [CLI](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/cli.md) is one file for Node 24; where Node 24 is missing, the installer offers a private copy for atira alone. `atira login` opens the browser, where you approve a token for this computer. On macOS and Linux, the second line puts `atira` on your PATH in this terminal; add it to your shell's startup file to keep it. Optional: connect your coding agent ([MCP](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/mcp.md)), and it starts test runs, reads logs and sees each browser's screen itself. Or skip the install: point a coding agent at [https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/llms.txt](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/llms.txt).

docs/reference/atira-llms-full.txt:154:Fork the starter kit, or build your own from the [run contract](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/run-contract.md) in any language, framework or architecture. The kit is a minimal Python skeleton, not an agent: it reads the run and submits an answer (`run.py`), attaches to the run's browsers (`browsers.py`), shows one call to each hosted model (`models.py`), and leaves your agent to `solve()` in `agent.py`.

docs/reference/atira-llms-full.txt:173:You need uv for the starter kit ([install uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/)); open a new terminal after installing it. Terminal 1: start the free models with `atira models proxy` and leave it open. Terminal 2: run the lines below. `atira scout --env` gives your agent the scouting logins, the way a run gets its own, and a browser opens on your machine. Nothing done here counts. With these logins, an answer entered on the tender portal is acknowledged but never counts. When it works, `atira test-run` runs it in the sandbox for up to 2 hours and opens the run live, with the score and full breakdown. Details: [how a run works](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/run-contract.md).
docs/reference/atira-llms-full.txt:191:Qwen3.8-Flash-Next and Cloudflare Clef work here too, with the same variables as in a run: [how to call them](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/start#models).
docs/reference/atira-llms-full.txt:195:The same sandbox as scored runs, on the public dataset: watch the browser and the live logs, and replay the recording afterwards. The hosted models need no key; a key of your own goes in a team secret on [your team page](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/team); only the timed run step gets it.
docs/reference/atira-llms-full.txt:203:A coding agent reviews the package, it runs once on the public dataset, and the result lands on the [leaderboard](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/challenges/rfq/leaderboard). One submission in flight at a time; your best one holds your place, and your latest one that passed review goes into the final run. [Submitting in full](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/submitting.md).
docs/reference/atira-llms-full.txt:211:We host Qwen3.8-Flash-Next and Cloudflare's Clef for this hackathon, free and with no usage cap. On your laptop, `atira models proxy` gives you a URL and key (setup on [your team page](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/team#team-models)). In test and scored runs it's set up for you. Free for you. Each call still adds its simulated price to your run's cost, so the cost ranking stays fair.
docs/reference/atira-llms-full.txt:295:| Fair play | The answer must come from the websites at run time, found by a model that does the navigating and deciding, not a fixed script or a crawler. A coding agent reviews every package. The final run uses a private dataset: the same jobs, bid rules and answer format, on different websites with other content and data. [Full rules](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/fair-play.md). |
docs/reference/atira-llms-full.txt:309:On the leaderboard's plot, each dot is a team, quality against cost or time. The dotted line is the Pareto front. The quickest and cheapest passing solution might also get a small prize ;) [Answers and scoring](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/scoring.md) has every point.

docs/reference/atira-llms-full.txt:463:Develop on your machine against the public websites with the scouting logins (`atira scout --env`), then test in the sandbox: `atira test-run` uploads your package, starts a test run and opens it live, or drop the package on [your team page](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/team). docs/reference/atira-llms-full.txt:517:Every model call goes through the platform's metering proxy, which records its tokens and cost; the hosted models need no key, and any other provider takes the team's own. docs/reference/atira-llms-full.txt:521:We host Qwen3.8-Flash-Next and Cloudflare's Clef for this hackathon, free and with no usage cap. On your laptop, `atira models proxy` gives you a URL and key (setup on [your team page](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/team#team-models)). In test and scored runs it's set up for you. Free for you. Each call still adds its simulated price to your run's cost, so the cost ranking stays fair.
docs/reference/atira-llms-full.txt:607:Put `agent.json` at the root of the tarball, next to your code and its dependency file. Up to 20 MB compressed. `setup` installs dependencies with network access, within 5 minutes that don't count toward your time; `run` is timed and reaches only the platform and the websites. `"browsers": 1–4` (default 1) is how many browsers the sandbox starts, each on its own screen. `"models"` lists the hosted models your agent calls; the run waits only for those to warm up (for all of them when it's absent). Node 24 with pnpm and bun, Python 3.12 with uv, and Rust with cargo are installed. The [starter kit](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/starter-kit.tar.gz) is a minimal skeleton to start from.
docs/reference/atira-llms-full.txt:619:Or drop the tarball on [your team page](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/team). Upload it as a test run first to watch it work in the sandbox: its browser live, its logs, and a recording afterwards.

docs/reference/atira-llms-full.txt:105:Your agent reads a public tender, finds the current specification, checks prices and stock in the ERP, looks up the approved discount in the sales inbox and submits one signed bid. Bring any frontier model, your own tools and prompts, up to four browsers in parallel; no human in the loop. Or use [ours](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/start#models): unlimited Qwen3.8-Flash-Next and Cloudflare Clef inference. Free for you. Each call still adds its simulated price to your run's cost, so the cost ranking stays fair. Every scored submission runs once on the public dataset. Eligible answers rank first, then higher quality, then lower cost × time. When the hackathon ends, every team's latest submission that passed review runs once by default, or best of three if the team opts in before the final run starts, on a private dataset. We pick the winners on three things, roughly in this order: performance on the private dataset, performance on the public dataset, and the elegance of the system.
docs/reference/atira-llms-full.txt:113:[Sign in with GitHub](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/login?next=/team) and create a team of up to 5. Invite teammates by their GitHub username on [your team page](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/team); each invite works only for that account.
docs/reference/atira-llms-full.txt:117:The [CLI](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/cli.md) is one file for Node 24; where Node 24 is missing, the installer offers a private copy for atira alone. `atira login` opens the browser, where you approve a token for this computer. On macOS and Linux, the second line puts `atira` on your PATH in this terminal; add it to your shell's startup file to keep it. Optional: connect your coding agent ([MCP](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/mcp.md)), and it starts test runs, reads logs and sees each browser's screen itself. Or skip the install: point a coding agent at [https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/llms.txt](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/llms.txt).

docs/reference/atira-llms-full.txt:154:Fork the starter kit, or build your own from the [run contract](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/run-contract.md) in any language, framework or architecture. The kit is a minimal Python skeleton, not an agent: it reads the run and submits an answer (`run.py`), attaches to the run's browsers (`browsers.py`), shows one call to each hosted model (`models.py`), and leaves your agent to `solve()` in `agent.py`.

docs/reference/atira-llms-full.txt:173:You need uv for the starter kit ([install uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/)); open a new terminal after installing it. Terminal 1: start the free models with `atira models proxy` and leave it open. Terminal 2: run the lines below. `atira scout --env` gives your agent the scouting logins, the way a run gets its own, and a browser opens on your machine. Nothing done here counts. With these logins, an answer entered on the tender portal is acknowledged but never counts. When it works, `atira test-run` runs it in the sandbox for up to 2 hours and opens the run live, with the score and full breakdown. Details: [how a run works](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/run-contract.md).
docs/reference/atira-llms-full.txt:191:Qwen3.8-Flash-Next and Cloudflare Clef work here too, with the same variables as in a run: [how to call them](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/start#models).
docs/reference/atira-llms-full.txt:195:The same sandbox as scored runs, on the public dataset: watch the browser and the live logs, and replay the recording afterwards. The hosted models need no key; a key of your own goes in a team secret on [your team page](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/team); only the timed run step gets it.
docs/reference/atira-llms-full.txt:203:A coding agent reviews the package, it runs once on the public dataset, and the result lands on the [leaderboard](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/challenges/rfq/leaderboard). One submission in flight at a time; your best one holds your place, and your latest one that passed review goes into the final run. [Submitting in full](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/submitting.md).
docs/reference/atira-llms-full.txt:211:We host Qwen3.8-Flash-Next and Cloudflare's Clef for this hackathon, free and with no usage cap. On your laptop, `atira models proxy` gives you a URL and key (setup on [your team page](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/team#team-models)). In test and scored runs it's set up for you. Free for you. Each call still adds its simulated price to your run's cost, so the cost ranking stays fair.
docs/reference/atira-llms-full.txt:295:| Fair play | The answer must come from the websites at run time, found by a model that does the navigating and deciding, not a fixed script or a crawler. A coding agent reviews every package. The final run uses a private dataset: the same jobs, bid rules and answer format, on different websites with other content and data. [Full rules](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/fair-play.md). |
docs/reference/atira-llms-full.txt:309:On the leaderboard's plot, each dot is a team, quality against cost or time. The dotted line is the Pareto front. The quickest and cheapest passing solution might also get a small prize ;) [Answers and scoring](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/scoring.md) has every point.

docs/reference/atira-llms-full.txt:463:Develop on your machine against the public websites with the scouting logins (`atira scout --env`), then test in the sandbox: `atira test-run` uploads your package, starts a test run and opens it live, or drop the package on [your team page](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/team). docs/reference/atira-llms-full.txt:517:Every model call goes through the platform's metering proxy, which records its tokens and cost; the hosted models need no key, and any other provider takes the team's own. docs/reference/atira-llms-full.txt:521:We host Qwen3.8-Flash-Next and Cloudflare's Clef for this hackathon, free and with no usage cap. On your laptop, `atira models proxy` gives you a URL and key (setup on [your team page](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/team#team-models)). In test and scored runs it's set up for you. Free for you. Each call still adds its simulated price to your run's cost, so the cost ranking stays fair.
docs/reference/atira-llms-full.txt:607:Put `agent.json` at the root of the tarball, next to your code and its dependency file. Up to 20 MB compressed. `setup` installs dependencies with network access, within 5 minutes that don't count toward your time; `run` is timed and reaches only the platform and the websites. `"browsers": 1–4` (default 1) is how many browsers the sandbox starts, each on its own screen. `"models"` lists the hosted models your agent calls; the run waits only for those to warm up (for all of them when it's absent). Node 24 with pnpm and bun, Python 3.12 with uv, and Rust with cargo are installed. The [starter kit](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/starter-kit.tar.gz) is a minimal skeleton to start from.
docs/reference/atira-llms-full.txt:619:Or drop the tarball on [your team page](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/team). Upload it as a test run first to watch it work in the sandbox: its browser live, its logs, and a recording afterwards.

docs/reference/atira-llms-full.txt:105:Your agent reads a public tender, finds the current specification, checks prices and stock in the ERP, looks up the approved discount in the sales inbox and submits one signed bid. Bring any frontier model, your own tools and prompts, up to four browsers in parallel; no human in the loop. Or use [ours](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/start#models): unlimited Qwen3.8-Flash-Next and Cloudflare Clef inference. Free for you. Each call still adds its simulated price to your run's cost, so the cost ranking stays fair. Every scored submission runs once on the public dataset. Eligible answers rank first, then higher quality, then lower cost × time. When the hackathon ends, every team's latest submission that passed review runs once by default, or best of three if the team opts in before the final run starts, on a private dataset. We pick the winners on three things, roughly in this order: performance on the private dataset, performance on the public dataset, and the elegance of the system.
docs/reference/atira-llms-full.txt:113:[Sign in with GitHub](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/login?next=/team) and create a team of up to 5. Invite teammates by their GitHub username on [your team page](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/team); each invite works only for that account.
docs/reference/atira-llms-full.txt:117:The [CLI](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/cli.md) is one file for Node 24; where Node 24 is missing, the installer offers a private copy for atira alone. `atira login` opens the browser, where you approve a token for this computer. On macOS and Linux, the second line puts `atira` on your PATH in this terminal; add it to your shell's startup file to keep it. Optional: connect your coding agent ([MCP](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/mcp.md)), and it starts test runs, reads logs and sees each browser's screen itself. Or skip the install: point a coding agent at [https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/llms.txt](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/llms.txt).

docs/reference/atira-llms-full.txt:154:Fork the starter kit, or build your own from the [run contract](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/run-contract.md) in any language, framework or architecture. The kit is a minimal Python skeleton, not an agent: it reads the run and submits an answer (`run.py`), attaches to the run's browsers (`browsers.py`), shows one call to each hosted model (`models.py`), and leaves your agent to `solve()` in `agent.py`.

docs/reference/atira-llms-full.txt:173:You need uv for the starter kit ([install uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/)); open a new terminal after installing it. Terminal 1: start the free models with `atira models proxy` and leave it open. Terminal 2: run the lines below. `atira scout --env` gives your agent the scouting logins, the way a run gets its own, and a browser opens on your machine. Nothing done here counts. With these logins, an answer entered on the tender portal is acknowledged but never counts. When it works, `atira test-run` runs it in the sandbox for up to 2 hours and opens the run live, with the score and full breakdown. Details: [how a run works](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/run-contract.md).
docs/reference/atira-llms-full.txt:191:Qwen3.8-Flash-Next and Cloudflare Clef work here too, with the same variables as in a run: [how to call them](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/start#models).
docs/reference/atira-llms-full.txt:195:The same sandbox as scored runs, on the public dataset: watch the browser and the live logs, and replay the recording afterwards. The hosted models need no key; a key of your own goes in a team secret on [your team page](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/team); only the timed run step gets it.
docs/reference/atira-llms-full.txt:203:A coding agent reviews the package, it runs once on the public dataset, and the result lands on the [leaderboard](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/challenges/rfq/leaderboard). One submission in flight at a time; your best one holds your place, and your latest one that passed review goes into the final run. [Submitting in full](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/submitting.md).
docs/reference/atira-llms-full.txt:211:We host Qwen3.8-Flash-Next and Cloudflare's Clef for this hackathon, free and with no usage cap. On your laptop, `atira models proxy` gives you a URL and key (setup on [your team page](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/team#team-models)). In test and scored runs it's set up for you. Free for you. Each call still adds its simulated price to your run's cost, so the cost ranking stays fair.
docs/reference/atira-llms-full.txt:295:| Fair play | The answer must come from the websites at run time, found by a model that does the navigating and deciding, not a fixed script or a crawler. A coding agent reviews every package. The final run uses a private dataset: the same jobs, bid rules and answer format, on different websites with other content and data. [Full rules](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/fair-play.md). |
docs/reference/atira-llms-full.txt:309:On the leaderboard's plot, each dot is a team, quality against cost or time. The dotted line is the Pareto front. The quickest and cheapest passing solution might also get a small prize ;) [Answers and scoring](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/scoring.md) has every point.

docs/reference/atira-llms-full.txt:607:Put `agent.json` at the root of the tarball, next to your code and its dependency file. Up to 20 MB compressed. `setup` installs dependencies with network access, within 5 minutes that don't count toward your time; `run` is timed and reaches only the platform and the websites. `"browsers": 1–4` (default 1) is how many browsers the sandbox starts, each on its own screen. `"models"` lists the hosted models your agent calls; the run waits only for those to warm up (for all of them when it's absent). Node 24 with pnpm and bun, Python 3.12 with uv, and Rust with cargo are installed. The [starter kit](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/starter-kit.tar.gz) is a minimal skeleton to start from.

Usage: atira eval <init|dev|deploy|preview|run|runs|board|ls|status|source|public|private|rm> ...

Team evals: write the starter kit, run an eval here with local scoring, deploy it and get its live URLs, run your agent on it, see your runs and its leaderboard; atira eval --help lists each

Subcommands:
  atira eval init [dir]
      Write the eval starter kit (four sites, a bid configurator, BRIEF.md, expected.json) to a new folder (default my-eval)
  atira eval dev [dir] [--port <first>] [--no-build] [--env]
      Run the eval here: build and start it on 127.0.0.1:8710… with the platform's environment and a local stand-in for its endpoints, which accepts the printed logins and scores each answer the app hands in against expected.json; --env prints the exports for your agent from another terminal
  atira eval deploy [dir] [--public] [--slug <slug>] [--title <title>] [--no-preview] [--dry-run]
      Check the eval and upload it: the first deploy creates it (private; its id goes in .atira/eval.json), later ones push a new version. Streams the build, then prints the world's public URLs and a preview login per site; --public publishes it
  atira eval preview [<eval>] [--hours <1-8>]
      The eval's live preview: the eval's one world's public URLs with the preview's login per site, and the latest answer's score; hands out new logins when none is live (nothing boots or restarts)
  atira eval run [<eval>] [--repeats <1-3>] [--package submission|test|sub_...|run_...|<dir>] [--label <name>]
      Run your agent on the eval's current version: your latest submission's package (default), your latest test run's, any earlier submission's or run's of your team by its id, or a folder
  atira eval runs [<eval>]
      Your team's entries on an eval (or on every eval): status, mean quality ± sd over the repeats, mean cost and time
  atira eval board [<eval>] [--version <evv_...>]
      A public eval's leaderboard for one version (default the current): each team's best entry, mean quality ± sd, mean cost and time
  atira eval ls
      Your team's evals and every public one: slug, id, visibility, owner, current version and the latest build
  atira eval status [<eval>]
      An eval and its versions with their builds; the latest build's log when it isn't ready
  atira eval source [<eval>] [--out <dir>] [--version <evv_...>]
      The files of an eval's version (yours, or any public one); --out writes them to a new folder, ready for atira eval dev and a deploy of your own
  atira eval public [<eval>]
      Publish an eval: every team can run on it and read its source, expected.json included; it gets a leaderboard
  atira eval private [<eval>]
      Make an eval private again: only your team sees it and runs on it
  atira eval rm [<eval>] [--yes]
      Delete an eval: its previews stop; its runs and their scores stay. Asks first, or takes --yes

<eval> is an eval's id (ev_...) or slug; in an eval's folder it defaults to the one in .atira/eval.json.
Guide: https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/evals.md

Team evals: write the starter kit, run an eval here with local scoring, deploy it and get its live URLs, run your agent on it, see your runs and its leaderboard; atira eval --help lists each

Subcommands:
  atira eval init [dir]
      Write the eval starter kit (four sites, a bid configurator, BRIEF.md, expected.json) to a new folder (default my-eval)
  atira eval dev [dir] [--port <first>] [--no-build] [--env]
      Run the eval here: build and start it on 127.0.0.1:8710… with the platform's environment and a local stand-in for its endpoints, which accepts the printed logins and scores each answer the app hands in against expected.json; --env prints the exports for your agent from another terminal
  atira eval deploy [dir] [--public] [--slug <slug>] [--title <title>] [--no-preview] [--dry-run]
      Check the eval and upload it: the first deploy creates it (private; its id goes in .atira/eval.json), later ones push a new version. Streams the build, then prints the world's public URLs and a preview login per site; --public publishes it
  atira eval preview [<eval>] [--hours <1-8>]
      The eval's live preview: the eval's one world's public URLs with the preview's login per site, and the latest answer's score; hands out new logins when none is live (nothing boots or restarts)
  atira eval run [<eval>] [--repeats <1-3>] [--package submission|test|sub_...|run_...|<dir>] [--label <name>]
      Run your agent on the eval's current version: your latest submission's package (default), your latest test run's, any earlier submission's or run's of your team by its id, or a folder
  atira eval runs [<eval>]
      Your team's entries on an eval (or on every eval): status, mean quality ± sd over the repeats, mean cost and time
  atira eval board [<eval>] [--version <evv_...>]
      A public eval's leaderboard for one version (default the current): each team's best entry, mean quality ± sd, mean cost and time
  atira eval ls
      Your team's evals and every public one: slug, id, visibility, owner, current version and the latest build
  atira eval status [<eval>]
      An eval and its versions with their builds; the latest build's log when it isn't ready
  atira eval source [<eval>] [--out <dir>] [--version <evv_...>]
      The files of an eval's version (yours, or any public one); --out writes them to a new folder, ready for atira eval dev and a deploy of your own
  atira eval public [<eval>]
      Publish an eval: every team can run on it and read its source, expected.json included; it gets a leaderboard
  atira eval private [<eval>]
      Make an eval private again: only your team sees it and runs on it
  atira eval rm [<eval>] [--yes]
      Delete an eval: its previews stop; its runs and their scores stay. Asks first, or takes --yes

<eval> is an eval's id (ev_...) or slug; in an eval's folder it defaults to the one in .atira/eval.json.
Guide: https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/evals.md

cat > dev/evals/diagnostics/HOSTED-AUTH-FAILURE.md <<'MD'
# Hosted eval authentication failure

The first development agent run `run_4ecb248a3470364d` cannot provide a valid
quality/performance comparison because none of the four sites authenticated.
No replacement agent runs were started by this diagnostic task.

A fresh platform preview `pv_af1f788ed294d0f8` targets the exact current development
version `evv_d920a5c072b9084d80fe` of eval `ev_25cdea6d26f33fa1`. Its API response
contains nonempty `name`, `url`, `username`, and `password` strings for `tender`,
`specification`, `erp`, and `mail`, matching the four manifest names. Usernames
have the documented preview `p_` prefix. The probe submits the exact returned
username/password strings through the actual rendered form using URL encoding;
there is no trimming, regeneration, or credential substitution.

All four login pages return HTTP 200. All four login POSTs return HTTP 200 with
an invalid-login page. The adapter's upstream `/v1/eval-worlds/verify` response is
HTTP **401**, for both Python urllib and an equivalent request using the official
Node `fetch` transport. Explicit User-Agent and both accepted bearer/header
forms do not change the failure. The hosted error message's retained vocabulary
contains **login** and **site**, and excludes token/bearer/world/version/expiry
terms. The full message was intentionally not exposed by the deployed diagnostic
instrumentation, so its exact wording is unavailable here. We cannot honestly
name an exact server-side cause from those two words.

A separate read-only request with a personal token confirms the endpoint's
invalid-world-token error is `authentication_error: invalid eval world token`,
which differs from the hosted login/site rejection. This supports a valid world
bearer reaching the login check, rather than a transport or User-Agent failure.
The official OpenAPI contract requires `{site, username, password}` and limits
successful verification to credentials on the world token's current version;
the preview and current version IDs in this reproduction match.

To reproduce using an existing preview response saved in an ignored private
file, without printing credentials:

```sh
python3 dev/evals/diagnostics/probe_hosted_auth.py PRIVATE_PREVIEW_RESPONSE.json
```

The resulting sanitized report is `hosted-auth-result.json`. The probe makes
only login GET/POST requests. It does not submit a bid, read expected answers,
mint new previews, launch an agent run, or cancel any backend run.

Required next step: inspect the platform's verification rejection for this eval,
version, preview and site names, including how each emitted login is attached to
the current version/site. If the platform expects a different site identifier,
that identifier must be returned/documented in the preview/run contract. If the
preview logins are associated with the wrong credential store/version, the
platform must correct that association. A hosted `/verify` 200 with its expected
preview ID on all four sites is required before another agent comparison.

The Node fallback in this current version is temporary diagnostic
instrumentation, invoked only after a read-only verify 401. It is not a proposed
permanent performance path, and never retries the answer endpoint. Six holdout
versions and the locale version remain untouched after the original deployment.
All eight worlds remain private and preserved. There is no further redeployment
planned until a concrete protocol correction is identified.
MD","max_output_tokens":3000}));
